extracted.intended_audience: Users of the Singular computer algebra system (especially those using the interactive interface and/or Emacs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for interactively running and configuring the Singular computer-algebra system (ASCII and Emacs interfaces): how to start/stop, interpret prompts, use online help, edit input, set command-line options, customize the Emacs interface, run demos, and troubleshoot common issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminate every command with a semicolon
rubrics_metrics.description: Every command has to be terminated by a ; (semicolon) followed by a RETURN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Singular will use the continuation prompt . when parts of a command are missing (e.g., missing semicolon). Semicolons inside strings are not interpreted as command terminators. Additional semicolons are treated as empty statements and harmless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start and exit Singular (ASCII and Emacs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start Singular in ASCII-terminal by entering Singular; start the Emacs UI by entering ESingular or M-x singular in Emacs. To exit Singular type quit;, exit; or $ (in Emacs prefer C-c $).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Singular and ESingular may be started with command-line options and filenames: Singular [options] [file1 [file2 ...]] and ESingular [options] [file1 [file2 ...]]. See Emacs-specific commands (e.g., ESingular) for Emacs-start details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret the SINGULAR prompt
rubrics_metrics.description: The main prompt > asks for new commands; the continuation prompt . requests missing parts of a command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Singular waits for blocks ({ ... }) to be closed and for unmatched quotes or braces before returning to >. If no regular prompt appears after a semicolon, Singular may be waiting for a " or }.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the online help system via help / ?
rubrics_metrics.description: Invoke the online help system with help or ?; help; shows the manual top, help topic; shows documentation on a topic which may be a function name or any index entry and may contain wildcards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help output can be displayed using various help browsers (html, builtin, emacs, dummy) or external browsers configured in LIB/help.cnf. Use help topic; and wildcards; see Section 5.1.52 for more info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Configure help browser and related environment variables
rubrics_metrics.description: The browser used for displaying help can be set with the command-line option --browser=<browser> or via system("--browser", "<browser>"). If no browser is set the first available in LIB/help.cnf is chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set default browser in $HOME/.singularrc. If local HTML pages are unavailable and --allow-net is set, HTML pages may be fetched from http://www.singular.uni-kl.de/Manual. Alternative locations can be set with SINGULAR_HTML_DIR and SINGULAR_INFO_FILE (for info-based browsers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Troubleshoot help browsers and required programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain external files/programs are required for help browsers (e.g., xinfo needs xterm and info). Under Unix the DISPLAY variable must be set for X11 browsers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If help browser cannot find local html pages and --allow-net is not set, configure LIB/help.cnf or set environment variables. If necessary, change entries in LIB/help.cnf to point to installed programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Info-based help navigation commands
rubrics_metrics.description: For info help browsers (tkinfo, xinfo, info, builtin) use single-character commands to navigate nodes and menus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common commands: q to quit, n/p/u for next/previous/up node, m to pick menu item by name, f to follow cross reference, l to return to original node, SPACE/DEL to page, s to search, numeric keys to pick subtopics, TAB to complete input, h for help, CTRL-H for overview, Ctrl-X 0 to remove extra window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrupt behavior (CTRL-C / C-c C-c)
rubrics_metrics.description: On Unix-like systems and Windows NT, typing CTRL-C (or C-c C-c in Emacs) interrupts Singular. The interpreter prints the current command and line and prompts for further action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options after interrupt: a (returns to top level after finishing current kernel command — kernel commands cannot be aborted), c (continue), q (quit). Note: (a)bort only applies when the interpreter, not the kernel, is active.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command-line input editing keys and history
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide command-line editing and history retrieval via keys: TAB (completion), CTRL-B/F (cursor left/right), CTRL-A/E (line begin/end), CTRL-D (delete under cursor, EOF on empty line), BACKSPACE/DELETE, CTRL-K/U (kill line parts), CTRL-N/P (next/previous history), RETURN sends line to parser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When run in ASCII-terminal, Singular will try to dynamically link with GNU Readline to provide enhanced features (history completion). If SINGULARHIST is set to a filename, history is stored across sessions; otherwise history is only per session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary command-line options (behavior control)
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular supports many command-line options to control behavior; general ones include -d/--sdb (enable source debugger), -e/--echo[=VAL] (set echo), -h/--help (print options help), --allow-net (allow help browsers to fetch HTML from net), --browser="VAL" (choose browser).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults differ by platform (e.g., default browser html on Windows). Use system("--long option name") to check values at runtime and system("--long option name string", expression) to redefine while running.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options to suppress or change output & startup behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Options include --no-rc (do not execute .singularrc), --no-stdlib (do not load standard.lib), --no-warn (suppress warnings), --no-out (suppress all output), --no-shell (restricted mode disallowing shell escape), -t/--no-tty (do not redefine terminal characteristics), -q/--quiet (suppress banner and redirect stderr to stdout).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use --no-rc or --no-stdlib to control which initialization actions occur. --quiet is useful when redirecting output to files. --no-shell restricts shell escapes and link-type objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timers, randomness, and related options
rubrics_metrics.description: Options include -r/--random=SEED to seed pseudo-random generator, --min-time=SECS to report only times larger than SECS, --ticks-per-sec=TICKS to set timer unit, and -v to print extended info about version/configuration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If --random not given, seed is time-based. Default --min-time is 0.5 seconds. Use --ticks-per-sec to change reported timer resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel/Batched mode options for ssi links
rubrics_metrics.description: Options for ssi links include -b/--batch (run in batch mode opening TCP/IP connection), --MPport=PORT (mandatory with --batch), --MPhost=HOST (mandatory with --batch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using --batch you must supply --MPport and --MPhost. See Section 4.9.5 for ssi link format and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESingular-specific command-line/environment options
rubrics_metrics.description: ESingular adds options: --emacs=EMACS (Emacs program), --emacs-dir=DIR (singular-emacs-home-directory), --emacs-load=FILE (load FILE on Emacs startup), --singular=PROG (start PROG as Singular within Emacs). Environment variables ESINGULAR_EMACS, ESINGULAR_EMACS_DIR, ESINGULAR_EMACS_LOAD, ESINGULAR_SINGULAR can also be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values from command line take priority over environment variables. ESingular inherits all Singular options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check and change option values at runtime
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of options (or their defaults) can be checked with system("--long option name").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example interactions: system("--quiet"); system("--min-time"); system("--random"); you can also redefine option values while running using system("--long option name string", expression).

rubrics_metrics.name: Startup sequence rules
rubrics_metrics.description: On start-up Singular: 1) loads standard.lib (unless --no-stdlib), 2) searches current, then home, then SearchPath for .singularrc and executes it (unless --no-rc), 3) executes the string from --execute, 4) executes files file1,file2,... given on the command line in order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: .singularrc files are appropriate for setting default command-line options and local customization; user .singularrc is found before system/global one and can override it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use .singularrc for default settings and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Put default browser or other options in $HOME/.singularrc to set defaults before first user input. Example: set system("--allow-net",1) if version >= 1306, or set browser to info unless running in Emacs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The .singularrc file is executed before first user input; be careful with syntax (final semicolon matters because of prompts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emacs interface recommended and its advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual recommends using the Emacs interface since it offers many more features: color highlighting, truncation of long lines, folding of input/output, TAB-completion for help topics, highlighting of matching parentheses, key-bindings and interactive menus, demo mode, convenient editing, and interactive customization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emacs (or XEmacs) version 20+ or XEmacs 20.3+ is required. ESingular is provided as an out-of-the-box solution that initializes the interface automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic Emacs concepts needed for Singular
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand Emacs notions: windows (panes), cursor/point, buffers (each file or the running Singular session is in a buffer), minibuﬀer for command input, and common window/buffer commands (C-x 1, C-x o, C-x b, C-x k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emacs commands generally use CONTROL (C-) or META (M-); use C-h t for Emacs tutorial. Use C-x C-c to exit Emacs (and Singular); C-g to stop unresponsive Emacs; mouse right-click for popup menus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting Singular in Emacs (ESingular vs M-x singular)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two ways: run ESingular to launch a new Emacs process that auto-initializes the Singular interface (.emacs-singular is used), or in an existing Emacs add load-path and autoload entries and run M-x singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESingular suppresses loading the user's .emacs and sets up defaults suitable for novices; if you prefer your own .emacs, add the suggested lisp snippet to enable M-x singular.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESingular initialization and customizable defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: ESingular automatically loads .emacs-singular and sets customizable variables to defaults giving a shell-like feeling; defaults can be changed (see customization) and saved either in $HOME/.emacs-singular-cust (ESingular) or appended to .emacs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESingular adds a Singular menu and (on XEmacs) a toolbar button. Customizations made in ESingular are not automatically taken over by a normal Emacs session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cygwin-specific notes for ESingular
rubrics_metrics.description: To run ESingular under Cygwin you need an X11 server (install xlaunch, emacs-X11, xterm and dependencies) and create a startup file that starts xterm; fork problems may require running /usr/bin/rebase-trigger full, stopping Cygwin processes and re-running setup-x86.exe and possibly rebooting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the described steps to resolve fork/rebase issues and ensure X11 server is available for the Emacs UI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emacs commands to start/stop/manage Singular processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Emacs interface defines commands: singular-other (start with prompts for executable, working dir, command line options, buffer name), singular (start with defaults), singular-exit-singular (C-c $) kills the process, singular-restart (C-c C-r) kills and restarts same args, singular-control-c (C-c C-c) interrupts and offers (a)bort/(q)uit/(r)estart/(c)ontinue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When starting a process in Emacs, a special startup file (~/.emacs-singularrc by default) is pasted into Singular at the end of the usual startup sequence; its name can be changed in customization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demo mode file format and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: A Singular demo file should consist of Singular commands separated by blank lines. Running a demo echoes input chunks up to the next blank line; pressing RETURN executes that chunk and shows output. Press RETURN on empty input to echo next chunk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can execute other commands while a demo is running (the next demo chunk will be echoed when you hit RETURN on an empty input line). Exit a demo with singular-demo-exit or start another demo to prematurely stop it. Demo mode behavior is customizable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customization of the Emacs interface via customize
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter customization with M-x customize (or via menu). The Singular interface customization buffer is divided into: Singular Faces, Singular Sections And Foldings, Singular Interactive Miscellaneous, and Singular Demo Mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change values interactively and save settings to a file to make them permanent. ESingular saves customized variables in $HOME/.emacs-singular-cust; running ESingular vs normal Emacs affects where settings are stored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Singular .sing and .lib files in Emacs (use C/C++ mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since Singular's language is similar to C, use Emacs C/C++-mode for .sing and .lib files to get automatic indentation, line-breaking and keyword highlighting; when running ESingular C/C++-mode is turned on automatically for these suffixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For normal Emacs sessions add auto-mode-alist entries for ".sing" and ".lib" to enable c++-mode, turn on font-lock-mode, enable auto-newline and hungry-delete, and consider the provided customize-face-at-point function for face customization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Useful Emacs key-bindings provided by the Singular Emacs mode
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual lists top Emacs/Singular commands and bindings such as singular (Start Default), singular-other (Start), singular-exit (C-c $), singular-restart (C-c C-r), singular-beginning-of-line (C-a moves past prompt), singular-dynamic-complete (TAB) for context-specific completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize with these bound commands for efficient interactive use; see the "Top 20 Emacs commands" section for more frequently used bindings.
